correctness.rationale: For positive a,b and 0<q<1, integrating the two exponential segments gives the stated log ratio, also at coincidence and at the terminal boundary. After writing F=x(1+ax+b)/[(1+ax)((1+aq)x+bq)], differentiation gives a positive denominator and numerator -b[ax^2-2aqx-q(1+b)]. The only positive root x* is strictly above q; clipping at 1 gives the unique constrained maximum including when x*=1. Evaluation at 1 gives the activation threshold. Evaluation at sqrt(q) gives q[a(1-2sqrt(q))-(1+b)], including the strict no-crossing result at a=1+b. In the crossing regime h_0<log(3)<log(4)<h_{1/2}. Factoring sqrt(q) out of the root gives both the derivative on the interior branch and the asymptotic offset. value.rationale: The restricted two-application problem is a useful deterministic benchmark. The threshold for any staggering and the stricter, sometimes nonexistent threshold for a late-season optimum distinguish three practically interpretable timing regimes. The exact sensitivity and midpoint offset say how scheduling changes with season length without reoptimization. This is mathematical value, not a prediction of crop yield or a recommendation for actual irrigation.
